provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: Order PDFs are written into the 'ftp/' directory (routes/order.ts:45). server.ts:294 then serves that same directory as a public browsable listing at '/ftp' using serveIndex. The only thing in front of it is 'serveIndexMiddleware'. Its name suggests a hook, not an authentication or authorization check, and nothing like security.isAuthorized() appears. The code even tags this line as the directoryListingChallenge vulnerability. This is the same pattern as the positive example: order documents written to a folder that anyone can list. The negative example avoids it by adding an auth check or writing to a private folder. Order PDFs are generated per customer and usually hold personal details such as the customer's email and what they ordered, so anyone who can reach '/ftp' can list and possibly open other customers' order documents. That breaks the requirement to control access to resources holding personal data. Two caveats: the Evidence doesn't show what goes into the PDF or what serveIndexMiddleware actually does, and the UserId model fields add nothing to this finding. Still, a public listing of the folder where order PDFs are written is enough to call this a true positive.
